genomeOverview.tagline: I build interfaces that load in milliseconds and scale to millions, preferably while no one's watching.

genes.name: Performance Optimization
genes.expression: I compulsively measure everything. Every component gets profiled, every bundle analyzed, every metric tracked. If it's not in Lighthouse, it didn't happen.
evidence: Reduced TTI from 4.2s to 890ms on e-commerce checkout
Implemented code-splitting strategy that cut initial bundle by 67%
Created custom React DevTools plugin to catch unnecessary re-renders

genes.name: TypeScript Architecture
genes.expression: I write types like a lawyer writes contracts. Every edge case covered, every null handled, every error path typed. Runtime errors are personal failures.
evidence: Migrated 120k LOC codebase from JavaScript to TypeScript with zero runtime errors
Created discriminated union system that eliminated 80% of type assertions
Authored TypeScript style guide adopted by 200+ engineers

genes.name: Accessibility Engineering
genes.expression: I test with screen readers not because it's required, but because 15% of users deserve working software. WCAG 2.1 AA is the floor, not the ceiling.
evidence: Achieved 100% keyboard navigation on complex data grid component
Fixed 47 ARIA violations in legacy component library
Implemented focus management system used across 30+ SPAs

genes.name: Documentation Systems
genes.expression: I'd rather write docs than explain the same thing twice. My PRs include decision records, my components include usage examples, my APIs include interactive playgrounds.
evidence: Created Storybook instance with 200+ component examples
Wrote architectural decision records (ADRs) for every major refactor
Maintained runbook that reduced onboarding time from 2 weeks to 3 days

genes.name: Asynchronous Communication
genes.expression: I thrive in async-first cultures. Written RFCs over meetings, Slack threads over calls, recorded demos over live presentations. My best work happens in 4-hour uninterrupted blocks.
evidence: Authored 23 technical RFCs with 95% approval rate
Reduced meeting load from 15hrs/week to 3hrs/week through async practices
Created PR template that eliminated 70% of review back-and-forth

genes.name: Solo Deep Work
genes.expression: I solve complex problems alone in a quiet room with noise-canceling headphones. Pair programming drains me. Open offices kill my productivity.
evidence: Rebuilt rendering engine solo over 3 months, delivered on time
Productivity metrics: 2x higher on full-remote vs hybrid schedule
Prefer code review over pair programming (review 50+ PRs/month)

genes.name: Process Adherence
genes.expression: I follow checklists religiously. Pre-commit hooks, CI/CD gates, PR templates, release processes - if it's automatable, I've automated it. If not, I've documented it.
evidence: Created pre-push checklist that caught 90% of bugs before CI
Set up ESLint config with 150+ rules, zero exceptions
Never missed a sprint deadline in 3 years

genes.name: Feedback Receptiveness
genes.expression: I take code review comments personally even though I know I shouldn't. Working on separating code quality from self-worth. Getting better at saying 'good catch' instead of 'but actually...'
evidence: Implemented blameless postmortem practice after production incident
Avg review response time: 2 hours (improving from 6 hours)
Started therapy to work on perfectionism

mutations.title: Bootcamp Graduate � Production Engineer
mutations.description: Transitioned from self-taught hobbyist to professional engineer through intensive bootcamp.
mutations.newTrait: Learned to let code speak for itself instead of apologizing for background
evidence: First production deploy: 99.98% uptime over 6 months
Won 'Best Code Quality' award from peer review metrics
Mentored 3 other bootcamp grads through onboarding

mutations.title: Feature Factory � Performance Team
mutations.description: Moved from shipping features to optimizing what already exists. Discovered love for benchmarking.
mutations.newTrait: Started measuring everything; realized fast software is good software
evidence: Reduced main bundle size by 2.1MB through lazy loading
Improved Core Web Vitals scores by 40% across all products
Created performance budgets enforced in CI

mutations.title: Office � Fully Remote
mutations.description: Company mandated RTO; I quit for fully-remote role. Productivity doubled overnight.
mutations.newTrait: Realized my best code comes from 4-hour focused sessions, not collaboration
evidence: GitHub contributions: 2800/year remote vs 1200/year office
Zero Slack messages on 'focus Fridays'
Delivered 3 major projects solo while previous team needed 4 people

projects.title: Checkout Flow Optimization
projects.context: E-commerce checkout had 23% cart abandonment rate. Users complained about 'loading forever.' Revenue team losing $2M/year.
approach: Profiled with Chrome DevTools: 4.2s TTI, 800ms of blocking JavaScript
Implemented route-based code splitting using React.lazy()
Moved analytics to web worker to free main thread

outcome.secondary: Cart abandonment dropped to 14.5%, +$800k annual revenue

testimonial.quote: Alex's optimization work directly improved our bottom line. The checkout flow now loads faster than our competitors.
testimonial.author: Sarah Kim, VP Product

projects.insight: Most performance problems aren't algorithmic - they're about lazy loading and deferring non-critical work.

projects.title: JavaScript � TypeScript Migration
projects.context: 120k LOC legacy JavaScript codebase. Production bugs traced to type errors. Team of 30 engineers needed type safety.
approach: Created incremental migration plan: 10% per sprint over 10 sprints
Built codemods to automate 60% of type annotations
Set up strict tsconfig.json with noImplicitAny
Held weekly 'TypeScript office hours' for team questions

outcome.metric: Zero runtime type errors in production after migration
outcome.secondary: 70% reduction in type-related bugs caught in code review

projects.insight: TypeScript adoption fails when it's all-or-nothing. Incremental migration with clear milestones wins.

projects.title: Data Grid Accessibility Overhaul
projects.context: Complex data table with sorting, filtering, pagination. Screen reader users couldn't use it. Legal team flagged ADA compliance risk.
approach: Audited with NVDA and VoiceOver: 47 ARIA violations found
Implemented ARIA grid pattern with row/cell semantics
Added keyboard shortcuts (arrow keys, Home/End, Page Up/Down)
Created focus management system with visible focus indicators

testimonial.quote: As a blind engineer, I can finally use our own product. This should be the standard.
testimonial.author: James Liu, Senior Engineer

projects.insight: Accessibility isn't a checklist - it's about testing with actual assistive tech and real users.

projects.title: Component Library Documentation Hub
projects.context: 200+ React components, zero documentation. Engineers re-inventing components instead of reusing. Onboarding took 2 weeks.
approach: Set up Storybook with MDX docs for every component
Created interactive examples with Storybook controls
Wrote migration guides for deprecated components
Added visual regression tests with Chromatic

outcome.metric: Onboarding time reduced from 2 weeks to 3 days
outcome.secondary: Component reuse rate increased from 40% to 85%

projects.insight: Good docs aren't just text - they're interactive examples developers can copy-paste.

uniqueSequence.statement: I build fast, accessible interfaces in isolation while writing documentation that helps others do the same.
whyRare: Most performance engineers ignore accessibility (adds overhead)
Most remote workers avoid documentation (prefer synchronous explanations)
Most introverts struggle with knowledge sharing (I weaponize writing)
evidence: Only engineer to achieve both 'Performance Award' and 'A11y Champion' recognition
Authored 200+ pages of internal docs with 4.8/5 satisfaction rating
Productivity 2x higher remote vs office despite zero pair programming

excel.name: Greenfield Performance Projects
excel.basis: Can architect for speed from day one without legacy constraints
excel.inPractice: Best work: building new checkout flow from scratch with performance budgets baked in
excel.bestApplied: Early-stage products where perf decisions compound; teams that measure Core Web Vitals

assumes: Performance budgets set before roadmap locks
Access to production telemetry and profiling tools

thrivesWhen: Benchmarks live in definition of done
Infra partners share real latency data weekly
amplifiers: Deep work sprints dedicated to load testing
CI gates enforcing Core Web Vitals
suppressors: Staging environments lack parity for perf tests

excel.name: Async-First Remote Teams
excel.basis: Low extraversion + high conscientiousness = written communication is superpower
excel.inPractice: Thrive in GitLab-style handbook cultures; struggle in 'let's hop on a quick call' environments
excel.bestApplied: Fully remote orgs with RFC culture, strong docs, and respect for deep work

thrivesWhen: Written updates celebrated over live standups
strugglesWhen: Peers expect instant responses all day
amplifiers: Recorded demos replace live status updates
suppressors: Camera-on meetings scheduled across time zones

excel.name: TypeScript Migrations
excel.basis: Combination of technical skill + process discipline + teaching through docs
excel.inPractice: Successfully led 3 migrations; patience for incremental progress + obsession with type safety
excel.bestApplied: Scaling startups moving from JS to TS; need someone who won't burn out team

assumes: Test coverage exists to catch regressions
strugglesIf: Team refuses to fix lint/type errors

thrivesWhen: Static analysis is part of CI
strugglesWhen: Shadow scripts bypass the build pipeline
Mixed JS/TS files stop strict mode adoption
amplifiers: Codemods + automated scaffolds ready to run

capable.name: Cross-Functional Collaboration
capable.basis: Can work with design/product, but drains energy battery quickly
capable.inPractice: Effective in structured meetings with clear agendas; struggle with open-ended brainstorming
capable.bestApplied: Teams with async-first practices; clear swim lanes between roles

strugglesIf: Roomful of stakeholders improvising in real time

suppressors: Back-to-back meetings stack with no breaks

capable.name: Mentoring Junior Engineers
capable.basis: Love teaching through docs/code review, struggle with live pairing
capable.inPractice: Write detailed PR feedback; maintain onboarding docs; hold office hours vs constant availability
capable.bestApplied: Async mentoring; written feedback; recorded demos

assumes: Predictable cadence for async office hours

thrivesWhen: I can batch-review PRs and Loom demos
amplifiers: Documented onboarding paths I can iterate

capable.name: Rapid Prototyping
capable.basis: Can move fast when needed, but quality suffers and I get anxious
capable.inPractice: Hackathons stress me out; prefer iterative refinement over 'ship and fix later'
capable.bestApplied: Projects with clear quality gates; time to refactor; not 'move fast break things' culture

assumes: Scope defined enough to avoid chaos
Quality guardrails exist even during sprints

thrivesWhen: Prototype handoff includes time to harden code
amplifiers: Pairing with PM who guards scope
Feature flags contain risk while iterating

developing.name: Public Speaking
developing.basis: Low extraversion + moderate neuroticism = conference talks are terrifying
developing.myApproach: Gave 2 internal talks (recorded, not live); working up to meetup presentations
developing.growth: Goal: Submit to 1 conference in 2025; started with writing blog posts to build confidence

assumes: Talks can be pre-recorded or tightly scripted
strugglesIf: Event requires me to improvise on stage

thrivesWhen: I rehearse with small trusted groups beforehand
Sessions allow slides + demos instead of panels
strugglesWhen: Emcee adds me to agenda last minute
Rooms are noisy with zero technical checks
amplifiers: Ability to publish talk as article afterward
suppressors: Mandatory live town halls with executives

developing.integrationGoal: Translate my async clarity into confident live storytelling without draining core introversion.

developing.name: Handling Ambiguity
developing.basis: High conscientiousness makes me crave clear requirements; struggle when specs are vague
developing.myApproach: Learning to ask clarifying questions earlier; building prototypes to explore options
developing.growth: Improved from 'blocked waiting for answers' to 'here are 3 options, which direction?'

assumes: Success criteria clarified before sprint one
PM partner iterates on specs with me
strugglesIf: Tasks drop in with zero context and instant deadlines

thrivesWhen: I can prototype multiple options then converge
strugglesWhen: People expect instant answers on undefined work
Meetings end with "we will figure it out later"
amplifiers: Access to users for quick feedback loops

developing.integrationGoal: Keep my conscientious planning while shipping exploratory spikes faster.

developing.name: Work-Life Balance
developing.basis: Perfectionism + remote work = tendency to over-work and burn out
developing.myApproach: Set hard stop at 6pm; no Slack on phone; therapy to address all-or-nothing thinking
developing.growth: Went from 60hr weeks to 45hr weeks; still working on truly disconnecting

assumes: Team respects async boundaries and offline hours

thrivesWhen: Workflows allow batching deep work earlier
suppressors: Chat apps on my phone buzzing 24/7

developing.integrationGoal: Protect my focus obsession while letting rest and recovery be part of the system.

thrivingEnvironments.title: Async-Remote with Deep Work Culture
thrivingEnvironments.why: Need 4-hour uninterrupted blocks to do my best work; written RFC culture plays to my strengths

thrivingEnvironments.title: Performance-First Engineering Teams
thrivingEnvironments.why: Love environments where speed is a feature; where Lighthouse scores are in CI/CD

thrivingEnvironments.title: Documentation-Driven Organizations
thrivingEnvironments.why: Thrive where 'write it down' is default; where onboarding is self-serve

strugglingEnvironments.title: Open Office + Meeting-Heavy Culture
strugglingEnvironments.why: Constant interruptions kill productivity; too many meetings drain energy for actual coding

strugglingEnvironments.title: Move Fast and Break Things
strugglingEnvironments.why: My conscientiousness rebels against 'ship now, fix later'; need time for quality and testing

strugglingEnvironments.title: Synchronous-First Teams
strugglingEnvironments.why: Real-time collaboration is exhausting; struggle in cultures where 'quick call' is default

compatibility.idealHabitat: Fully remote company with async-first culture, strong documentation practices, performance-focused engineering team, TypeScript codebase, and respect for deep work. Bonus: accessibility is a priority, not an afterthought.
